findings.title: Scanner pre-existing rescue never matches: real ubs prints absolute paths, and the baseline runs in a scratch dir
findings.evidence: Promise (close-gate.sh 531-538, FRICTIONS.md scanner-leg-has-no-baseline marked LANDED): a finding present at the base tree and at HEAD is pre-existing and does not refuse. Reality: sig_of keeps the path in the signature. The baseline ubs runs with `cd "$SCRATCH"` (a mktemp dir), and real ubs 0.x prints ABSOLUTE paths in its detail lines even when given a relative argument. I measured it: `ubs a.js` printed `/tmp/ubsprobe.3NfM/a.js:4  ...`. The same file scanned from `base/` printed `/tmp/ubsprobe.3NfM/base/a.js:4 ...`, and the two signature sets had 0 of 8 in common. So in production every HEAD finding counts as NEW and the rescue is dead code. AC4b passes only because the test's ubs mock (close-gate.test.sh:160) prints a RELATIVE `$f:$ln:1`, a shape real ubs never prints. Real ubs also prints `path:line` with no column (the mock always adds `:1`). The mock is wrong; the code was built to fit the mock.
findings.fix: Normalise the path before comparing: strip the "$PWD/" prefix from HEAD detail lines and the "$SCRATCH/" prefix from base detail lines (or key on the SCAN_FILES-relative path). Make the mock print absolute paths with no column so AC4b runs against the real shape. Also compare as a multiset (count each signature) instead of set membership: a bead that ADDS another identical finding would be rescued as pre-existing.

findings.title: Identity canon still says the conductor reads agent.name from the spawn and that stance children have no mcp tools; SKILL.md cites it for the opposite procedure
findings.evidence: ac-implement/SKILL.md:51 now builds the roster from `resource://agents/{project_key}` filtered by task_description, and cites agent-identity.md § Handing a name is a SPEC VIOLATION as canon. That canon (line 76) still says the conductor reads the minted name back from the spawn response's agent.name; line 39 says stance agents carry zero mcp__* tools and the conductor holds reservations on their behalf; line 138 says a stance child has no minted name and cannot reserve; line 147 (the ac-land roster sweep) says names are read back from agent.name. agents/implementer.md now carries macro_start_session, file_reservation_paths, release_file_reservations and deregister_agent.
findings.fix: Rewrite agent-identity.md lines 39, 76, 138 and 147: the implementer stance child mints its own name and reserves under it; the conductor's roster (and ac-land's) comes from agents registered since the run started, filtered by the run id in task_description.

findings.title: The human-gate-template close example records DECISION (operator), which the new gate refuses
findings.evidence: This diff edited the lines just below but left the ruling at line 226 as `DECISION (operator): option (a), OneSignal...`. close-gate.sh:205-212 now accepts only a name on `Humans who rule: Craig`, or ac-tidy on a pipeline-proposal bead. 'operator' is on neither, so the fenced example ends in CLOSE-REFUSED DECISION.
findings.fix: Change the example to `DECISION (Craig): ...` and add one sentence: the actor must be a name taken verbatim from bead-conventions.md's `Humans who rule:` line.

findings.title: Nothing ties the <human> placeholder to the canon line, and the gate strips spaces from the list but not from the actor
findings.evidence: ac-human action-loop.md:18 and bead-conventions.md:240 say `DECISION (<human>): ...` without saying which string fills <human>. The same action-loop file signs plan approval with `$(git config user.name)` = 'Craig van Heerden'. The gate runs `case ",${HUMANS// /}," in *",$RULING_ACTOR,"*)` — the list loses its spaces, RULING_ACTOR keeps them, so 'Craig van Heerden' never matches 'Craig'; a full name on the canon line becomes 'CraigvanHeerden', which no actor can match. A real human ruling through the documented tap is refused. No test covers a multi-word name.
findings.fix: Split HUMANS on commas, trim each entry, compare to the trimmed RULING_ACTOR keeping inner spaces. State in action-loop.md and bead-conventions.md that <human> is copied verbatim from `Humans who rule:`. Add cases for `DECISION (Craig van Heerden): ...` and a comma-plus-space canon list.

findings.title: The gate checks only the FIRST DECISION line, so an earlier unauthorized or superseded ruling blocks or overrides a later valid one
findings.evidence: `grep -m1` picks the first comment whose first line matches. Canon routes agents to record `DECISION (agent): ...` on human-gate beads they may enrich. A bead with an earlier `DECISION (agent)` then `DECISION (Craig)` is refused; with two Craig rulings the older one wins the landing record. Every ruling test has exactly one DECISION comment.
findings.fix: Iterate every first-line match and take the LAST authorized one. Add tests for [agent then Craig] (closes) and [Craig A then Craig B] (record cites B).

findings.title: The ac-tidy exception is documented as the literal 'moot' but accepts any ac-tidy ruling text
findings.evidence: close-gate.sh and bead-conventions.md say the only non-human ruling is `DECISION (ac-tidy): moot` on a pipeline-proposal bead. The code checks only actor=='ac-tidy' plus the label, so `DECISION (ac-tidy): option A — ship it` also closes — and ac-tidy itself files human-gate,pipeline-proposal decision beads (ac-tidy/SKILL.md:56).
findings.fix: Require `^DECISION \(ac-tidy\): moot( |$)` for the ac-tidy branch; add a refuse test for a non-moot ac-tidy ruling.

findings.title: The implementer's new tool list cannot carry out worker.md's renew, re-list and message steps
findings.evidence: worker.md §5b says renew on a long bead, verify release by re-listing, and message the holder on conflict. agents/implementer.md:4 grants only macro_start_session, file_reservation_paths, release_file_reservations and deregister_agent — no renew, no send_message, no listing.
findings.fix: Add renew_file_reservations and send_message (plus a listing tool) to the implementer tools, or cut §5b to what the stance can do.
